item.research_question: How can the metastability of the γ matrix in a dual-phase high entropy alloy be tuned via alloy chemistry and processing to achieve extremely high strength and sustained work hardening ability?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc-casting followed by multi-pass friction stir processing (M-pass) with 3 overlapping passes; rotational rates decremented from 650 RPM (pass 1) to 350 RPM (pass 2) to 250 RPM (pass 3) with Argon shrouding
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at an initial strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹
key_findings: The M-pass specimen exhibited a yield strength (YS) of 950 MPa and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 1.15 GPa.
Grain refinement via M-pass reduced grain size from 100 µm (as-cast) to 1.3 µm.
The as-cast material showed a YS of 400 MPa and ductility of 7%, while the M-pass specimen achieved 12% total elongation.
The work hardening rate (θ) for the M-pass specimen reached 3612 MPa at the onset of the transformation-dominated sub-stage.
In the as-cast condition, the γ phase fraction decreased from 94% to 11% after complete tensile deformation.
In the M-pass condition, the γ phase fraction decreased by approximately 90% after complete tensile deformation.
The M-pass specimen contained 88% γ phase and 12% ε phase prior to deformation, whereas the as-cast condition had a different phase distribution.
item.mechanism: The addition of Si decreases the stacking fault energy and increases the metastability of the γ matrix, promoting rapid γ → ε transformation (TRIP) and deformation twinning in the ε phase. The fine grain size (1.3 µm) provides high grain boundary area that exerts back stress, ensuring uniform strain partitioning between the γ and ε phases, which sustains the work hardening rate and prevents premature failure.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors propose that tuning the metastability of the γ phase by adding non-transition elements like Si is a new pathway for designing HEAs with higher strength and work hardenability, implying further exploration of this compositional strategy.
quotes: The addition of Si in DP-5Si-HEA decreased the stability of f.c.c. (γ) matrix thereby promoting pronounced transformation induced plastic deformation

Higher yet sustained WH ability in fine grained DP-5Si-HEA is associated with the uniform strain partitioning among the metastable γ phase and resultant h.c.p. (ε) phase thereby resulting in total elongation of 12%

Question: How can the metastability of the γ matrix in a dual-phase high entropy alloy be tuned via alloy chemistry and processing to achieve extremely high strength and sustained work hardening ability?. System: Fe42Mn28Co10Cr15Si5 (at.%) dual-phase high entropy alloy (DP-5Si-HEA). Processing: Vacuum arc-casting followed by multi-pass friction stir processing (M-pass) with 3 overlapping passes; rotational rates decremented from 650 RPM (pass 1) to 350 RPM (pass 2) to 250 RPM (pass 3) with Argon shrouding. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at an initial strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Mechanism: The addition of Si decreases the stacking fault energy and increases the metastability of the γ matrix, promoting rapid γ → ε transformation (TRIP) and deformation twinning in the ε phase. The fine grain size (1.3 µm) provides high grain boundary area that exerts back stress, ensuring uniform strain partitioning between the γ and ε phases, which sustains the work hardening rate and prevents premature failure..
